newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing debt market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing debt market report.

text.p: Dutch bonds surrendered strong gains to close lower in thin trading ahead of the Easter long weekend.
Dealers said guilder paper was marked down after U.S. Treasuries dived, pushing the U.S. 30 year yield up through the key seven percent level.
"I don't know what's behind it," said one dealer.
Another said: "It's not been dramatic. It just eased off."
But they saw strong buying interest in the June 2006 state loan which, they said, had appeared cheap relative to the guilder yield curve.
Guilder bonds had opened stronger and gained a few ticks through the morning before losing these gains as Treasuries dived.

Dealers said the sell-off may have been a late reaction ot negative U.S. data on Thursday and could have reflected concern about forthcoming statistics and the possibility of a further rise in interest rates.
The demand for 2006 Dutch paper was attributed to domestic professionals rather than institutional interest.
"A couple of big buyers were coming in," said a broker.
One dealer said the market have been short in the June 2006s.
